extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry (experts in fundamental groups, IUT/Mochizuki-related topics)
extracted.subtask_description: Algorithms and group-theoretic characterisations to reconstruct geometric/arithmetic fundamental groups, cusps, decomposition/inertia subgroups, and curve invariants (g, r) from profinite/pro-l arithmetic fundamental groups, mostly over number fields or p-adic (finite) extensions. Focused on mono-anabelian (model-free) reconstruction used in IUT-related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic characterisation of kernel N for number fields
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a number field and 1 -> N -> E -> G -> 1 is exact with N topologically finitely generated, then N is characterised in E as the maximal closed normal subgroup of E which is topologically finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 2.2 (1): every topologically finitely generated closed normal subgroup of Gal(Fbar/F) is trivial (cf. [FJ, Theorem 15.10]); this yields a purely group-theoretic identification of N inside E when F is a number field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamagawa condition Tam1 (coinvariant quotient Q finite free Z-module)
rubrics_metrics.description: For F a finite extension of Q_p, for each open subgroup E0 <= E write N0 := E0 ∩ N and G0 := E0/N0 and let Q := ((N0)^{ab})_{G0}/(tors). Tam1: for all sufficiently small open E0, Q is a finitely generated free Z-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition is part of Proposition 2.2 (2). Here ((N0)^{ab})_{G0} denotes the G0-coinvariants of the abelianisation; (tors) denotes torsion part. Tam1 is an assumption used to carry out the Tamagawa-type characterisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamagawa condition Tam2 (dimension equality and p-detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: With Tam1 assumed, N is characterised as the intersection of those open subgroups E0 <= E such that for any prime l ≠ p, a certain equality of l-adic and p-adic dimensions for (E0)^{ab} versus E^{ab} scaled by index [(E): (E0)] holds; moreover p is characterised as the unique prime where a related difference is nonzero for infinitely many l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 2.2 (2) states Tam2 explicitly as (dim_{Q_p}(...)/dim_{Q_l}(...)) ratios equalling the index [(E):(E0)] etc.; the equalities are equivalent to [F0: Q_p] = [(E):(E0)][F:Q_p], hence detect N and p group-theoretically using abelianisations and coinvariant ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tate module coinvariants finite free Z-module (Lemma 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be a non-Archimedean local field and A a semi-abelian variety over F. Writing T(A)=Hom(Q/Z, A(F)) for the Tate module, Q := T(A)^G/(tors) is a finitely generated free Z-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 2.3 provides the arithmetic input used to verify Tam1 in many cases: by splitting the semi-abelian variety into toric and abelian parts and using potential good reduction + Weil conjectures for abelian varieties, the G-coinvariants modulo torsion become a free Z-module of finite rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstruction of π1(X_F) inside π1(X) via Tam2
rubrics_metrics.description: For X a geometrically connected smooth hyperbolic curve over a finite extension F of Q_p, the subgroup π1(X_F) inside π1(X) (i.e., the kernel of arithmetic -> G_F) is group-theoretically characterised as in Proposition 2.2 (2) (Tam2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.4: the Tamagawa algorithm (Tam1/Tam2) applies to arithmetic fundamental group exact sequence 1 -> π1(X_F) -> π1(X) -> G_F -> 1, so the geometric subgroup can be reconstructed inside the arithmetic fundamental group using abelianisation dimension tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slim group (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A profinite group G is slim if for every open subgroup H ≤ G we have Z_G(H) = {1} (i.e., the centraliser of H in G is trivial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 2.5 (1). Slimness is a rigidness condition ensuring very few centralisers; it is used to deduce uniqueness/epimorphism properties for maps and to mirror geometric epimorphism behavior at the group level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative slimness over G2 via f (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f: G1 -> G2 continuous, G1 is relatively slim over G2 (via f) if for every open subgroup H ≤ G1 we have Z_{G2}(f(H)) = {1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 2.5 (2). This is a relative version of slimness which ensures images of open subgroups have trivial centraliser in the target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications between slimness and commensurable terminality
rubrics_metrics.description: If H ≤ G is relatively slim then both H and G are slim. If H ≤ G is commensurably terminal and H is slim then H is relatively slim in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 2.6 collects these formal implications; they are used to propagate slimness and to deduce properties of larger groups from subgroups and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/global decomposition groups are commensurably terminal and slim (Prop 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a number field F and a non-Archimedean place v, the decomposition group G_v ≤ G = Gal(Fbar/F) is commensurably terminal in G, relatively slim, and slim; moreover G itself is slim. For hyperbolic curves over F the geometric π1 and arithmetic π1 (and the local π1) are slim; inertia subgroups at cusps (and their pro-l quotients) are commensurably terminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 2.7 (1)+(2): uses local class field theory, Torelli, and Galois arguments. These structural properties are exploited to identify decomposition/inertia groups and to ensure group-theoretic algorithms behave like geometric coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: X not proper iff geometric π1 is free profinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyperbolic curve X over a local field is non-proper (i.e., has r>0 cusps) if and only if its geometric fundamental group π1(Xbar) is a free profinite group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 2.8 (1): this is a purely group-theoretic criterion to detect affineness (presence of cusps) from the profinite fundamental group via (non-)vanishing of H^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct genus g and number of cusps r from π1 using weight decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: One can recover (g,r) from the arithmetic fundamental group π1(X) by computing dimensions of Q_l-vector spaces coming from (π1)^{ab}⊗Q_l and extracting weight-zero and weight-two parts under Frobenius action; explicit formulas for r and g are given in Lemma 2.8 (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 2.8 (2) gives formulas: r = dim_{Q_l} ker(...) (weight=2) etc., and g expressed via dimensions of weight spaces. Requires reconstruction of G_k, p, q and Frobenius to define weights (these are group-theoretically reconstructible by prior propositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation of kernel of natural surjection by behavior of cusps under coverings
rubrics_metrics.description: An open subgroup H ≤ π1(X) is contained in ker(π1(X) -> π1(Xbar)) (or pro-l analogue) if and only if for the corresponding covering X_H one has r(X_H) = [π1(X): H] r(X) (i.e., the number of cusps scales multiplicatively by index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.9 (1): this gives a group-theoretic test (using the reconstructed r from Lemma 2.8) to decide when an open subgroup lies in the kernel to the geometric quotient by checking cusp counts on coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation of inertia subgroups in pro-l fundamental groups via vanishing of composites
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed subgroup A ≤ π1(X)^{(l)} is contained in the inertia subgroup of some cusp iff for every open subgroup H ≤ π1(X)^{(l)} the composite A ∩ H -> H^{ab} -> (H^{ab})_{G}/(tors) vanishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.9 (2): when A ≅ Z_l, membership in an inertia subgroup can be detected by the vanishing property in abelianised coinvariants of all finite-index subgroups corresponding to coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct set of cusps as conjugacy classes of pro-l inertia subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of cusps of X can be reconstructed as the π1(X)^{(l)}-orbits (conjugacy classes) of inertia subgroups A ≅ Z_l that satisfy the inertia-characterisation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.9 (3): uses (2) plus Proposition 2.7(2c) (commensurable terminality) to recover the global set of cusps from group theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct cusps of the universal pro-cover and inertia subgroups as stabilisers
rubrics_metrics.description: By functorially reconstructing cusps of every covering Y -> X from π1(Y) given inside π1(X), one reconstructs the cusps of the universal pro-cover eX -> X; inertia subgroups in π1(X) are precisely the subgroups which fix some cusp of eX determined by the basepoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.9 (4),(5): iterative reconstruction of cusps via all coverings yields the universal cusp set; inertia subgroups are then identified as stabiliser subgroups of those cusps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation of decomposition groups of cusps as normalizers of inertia
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition groups D of cusps in π1(X) (or π1(X)^{(l)}) are exactly the normalisers N_{π1(X)}(I) (resp. N_{π1(X)^{(l)}}(I)) for some inertia subgroup I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.9 (6): once inertia subgroups are reconstructed, their normalizers yield decomposition groups; uses commensurable terminality to ensure uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisation for l-cyclotomically full fields: reconstruct cyclotomic character and use filtrations
rubrics_metrics.description: For l-cyclotomically full fields (or under Delta'X), one can reconstruct a positive power of the l-adic cyclotomic character (up to finite-order character) from actions on torsion-free subgroups of π1^{ab}⊗Q_l, and then use filtrations of finite-dimensional Q_l[G_k]-modules (graded pieces either finite-quotient action or simple) to replace dim_{Q_l} weight-space counts in the reconstruction formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 2.9.2 sketches how the arguments generalise beyond strict MLF/NF hypotheses: reconstructing the cyclotomic character allows one to define weights and replicate the dimension-formula methods of Lemma 2.8; requires careful extraction of maximal power by which G_k acts in certain subquotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: sub-p-adic field
rubrics_metrics.description: A field k is sub-p-adic if it admits an injective embedding into some finitely generated field L over Q_p for some p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.1 (1). Examples include finite extensions of Q_p, finitely generated extensions of Q_p, finite extensions of Q, and certain compositum subfields of Qbar (see Remark 3.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Kummer-faithful field
rubrics_metrics.description: A characteristic-0 field k is Kummer-faithful if for every finite extension k' of k and every semi-abelian variety A over k', the Kummer map A(k') -> H^1(k', T(A)) is injective (equivalently: intersection of all nA(k') is {0}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.1 (2). This property ensures that rational points are detected by their Kummer images, and is a strong arithmetic rigidity property used in mono-anabelian arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: l-cyclotomically full field
rubrics_metrics.description: k is l-cyclotomically full if the l-adic cyclotomic character χ_{cyc,l}: G_k -> Z_l^× has open image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.1 (3). This property is used to control cyclotomic twists and define weight decompositions in l-adic representations arising from π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications among field properties and stability under finite generation
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is sub-p-adic then k is Kummer-faithful. If k is Kummer-faithful then k is l-cyclotomically full for any l. Kummer-faithfulness is preserved under taking finitely generated extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 3.2 proves these implications: embeddings into finitely generated Q_p-extensions reduce to the Q_p-case and use Weil restriction and structure of p-adic points of abelian varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Lock(X) and k-core (terminal object)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a geometrically normal, connected algebraic stack X over k, Lock(X) is the category of generically scheme-like stacks finite étale over some finite étale cover of X; X admits a k-core if Lock(X) has a terminal object (the k-core).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.3: existence of k-core (terminal object) is a stack-theoretic finiteness/terminality condition used to define elliptic admissibility and cuspidalisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: strictly Belyi type hyperbolic orbicurve
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyperbolic orbicurve X over k is strictly Belyi type if (a) X is defined over a number field, and (b) there are finite étale coverings X' -> X_0 -> X'' where X_0 is over a finite extension of k and X'' is a genus-0 hyperbolic curve over a finite extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.4 (1): 'strictly Belyi type' characterises orbicurves that, up to finite étale covers, map to genus 0 curves defined over number fields (Belyi-like condition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: elliptically admissible orbicurve
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyperbolic orbicurve X over k is elliptically admissible if X admits a k-core which is a semi-elliptic orbicurve (i.e., quotient of E \ {O} by ±1 in stack sense for an elliptic curve E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.4 (2): elliptic admissibility indicates that the terminal finite-étale object in Lock(X) is semi-elliptic; used to control special orbicurves in the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction hypotheses: (Delta)X, (GC), (slim), (Cusp)X, (Delta)'X
rubrics_metrics.description: (Delta)X: there is a group-theoretic characterisation of the geometric subgroup π1(Xbar) inside π1(X) (or equivalently the quotient π1(X)/π1(Xbar)). (GC): isom-version of relative Grothendieck conjecture — Isom_k(X,Y) -> Isom_{G_k}^{Out}(π1(Xbar), π1(Ybar)) bijective. (slim): G_k is slim. (Cusp)X: group-theoretic characterisation of decomposition groups of cusps in π1(X). (Delta)'X: either π1(X) quotient is given and (Delta)X holds, or both geometric and arithmetic π1 are given as input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.4.3 summarizes these conditions and their roles: (Delta)X, (GC), (slim), (Cusp)X are hypotheses under which mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithms are stated; the paper lists known cases where they hold (NF, MLF, sub-p-adic via Thm B.1, etc.). (Delta)'X emphasises whether the algorithm is allowed to assume π1(X) is already delineated inside π1(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of maps from slimness / inclusion maps are epimorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If G is slim and φ1, φ2: G -> H are open homomorphisms that agree after precomposing with some open subgroup image (i.e., φ1 ∘ ι = φ2 ∘ ι for an open ι: K -> G), then φ1 = φ2. Equivalently, inclusions of arithmetic π1 of a covering into that of the base are epimorphisms in the slim setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 3.5 and Remark 3.5.1: by replacing with normal open subgroups one deduces equality using triviality of centralisers; geometrically this mirrors that finite étale covers are epimorphisms and so the corresponding group inclusion behaves like an epimorphism when target is slim.
